title: Numbers with a sideways direction
question: What do you get when a number is allowed to square to minus one?
hook: Square any ordinary number and you never land below zero, so what could possibly square to minus one?
idea: Complex numbers add a second, sideways direction to the number line, and that is enough to solve every non-constant polynomial equation.

beats.prompt: In the 16th century, mathematicians met square roots of negative numbers while working on cubic equations. Every nonzero real number squares to a positive result, so these roots looked impossible. What did they do with them?

choices.label: Used them as a symbolic device, since they helped find real solutions
Dropped cubic equations until a purely real method turned up
choices.feedback: It tempts because the roots looked impossible, but the roots turned out to be helpful for real solutions, so people kept using them.

choices.label: Declared them fictitious, so they could never be used in real mathematics
choices.feedback: It tempts because of the name imaginary, but these numbers are no less valid than real numbers and are essential to science.

beats.explain: Such roots proved helpful for determining real solutions of cubic equations. At first they were treated as a mere symbolic contrivance, and in the 17th century they were named imaginary numbers.

beats.prompt: Match each operation or idea to what it means on the complex plane.
beats.explain: Each statement turns something done with numbers into something you can see on the plane.

beats.prompt: Sort each complex number by what kind of number it is.
beats.explain: A real number a is the complex number a + 0i, with imaginary part 0. A purely imaginary number bi is 0 + bi, with real part 0.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong. Which one?
steps: Positive times positive is positive, and negative times negative is also positive.
So every real number squares to something that is not negative.
So no real number squares to minus one.
So no number of any kind can, and such equations have no solutions anywhere.
beats.explain: Complex numbers allow solutions to all non-constant polynomial equations, including ones that have no solutions among the real numbers.
